subject.title: gh-issues skill: untrusted issue body injected directly into sub-agent prompt

question: Should this issue require both gh-issues runtime untrusted-content handling and accepted per-spawn child tool scoping before closure, or is prompt-level guidance plus existing global subagent policy sufficient under OpenClaw's trust model?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent fix changes model-facing skill execution, sessions_spawn API/session-state semantics, and the security-hardening versus vulnerability boundary.

options.title: Require runtime boundary and child scoping
options.body: Land or replace the open toolsAllow work and add gh-issues content wrapping, summarization, length limiting, or equivalent runtime isolation before treating this fixed.

options.title: Accept prompt-only hardening
options.body: Treat a narrower SKILL.md guidance update as sufficient defense-in-depth while documenting that hostile issue bodies remain inside the operator-granted agent trust boundary.

options.title: Defer unified delegated-agent policy
options.body: Keep this open until maintainers design one content and capability policy for skills, hooks, cron, and sessions_spawn.

recommendation.title: Require runtime boundary and child scoping
recommendation.body: Land or replace the open toolsAllow work and add gh-issues content wrapping, summarization, length limiting, or equivalent runtime isolation before treating this fixed.
